independent_solve.reasoning: During the absolute refractory period, the neuron is incapable of generating a second action potential regardless of the stimulus strength. This is primarily due to the inactivation of voltage-gated Na+ channels. These channels enter an 'inactivated' state at the peak of the action potential and remain in this state until the membrane potential repolarizes sufficiently to reset them to the 'closed' state. While K+ channels are involved in repolarization, the inability to open Na+ channels is the specific mechanism defining the absolute refractory period.
